title: Valorization of rice straw into value-added bio-composites through hybridization of field-retted jute fibre
content: Lignocellulosic fiber-reinforced polymer composites have emerged as environmentally friendly, sustainable alternatives to conventional composite materials, making them highly suitable for a wide range of structural and semi-structural applications in sustainable materials engineering. This research focuses on fiber length optimization, alkali surface treatment, and hybridization with jute fibers in rice straw fiber/epoxy composites. The rice straw-reinforced composites were fabricated with four fiber lengths (5 mm, 10 mm, 15 mm, and 20 mm) to evaluate the influence of fiber length on their mechanical performance. Among all the prepared composites, the R5 composite containing 5 mm rice straw fibers exhibited the highest tensile and flexural strengths, with corresponding values of 24.70 MPa and 43.16 MPa, respectively. After optimizing the fiber length, the rice straw and short jute fibers were treated with 3 wt% NaOH, increasing the tensile strength to 37.96 MPa (∼53.7%) and the flexural strength to 93.59 MPa (∼116.8%) compared with the untreated composite. This improvement was attributed to the partial removal of hemicellulose and lignin, which enhanced the fiber surface roughness and promoted stronger interfacial bonding between the fibers and the polymer matrix. As a result, the original tensile strength of 24.37 MPa was increased by ∼75.7% (43.39 MPa) through the improvement of loosely bound interfacial contact areas by hybridization with treated jute fibers. The flexural strength reached 66.74 MPa, indicating enhanced fiber–matrix bonding efficiency, which was primarily attributed to effective stress transfer and crack-bridging mechanisms between the short fibers and the stabilized polymer matrix. These improved interfacial interactions also increased the energy absorption capacity of the composites and reduced water uptake by 4.6% in the treated hybrid composites, thereby enhancing both impact resistance and water resistance.
